note: Hand-derived from CanonicalIAMCanPerformEdgeUpsertCypher (go/internal/storage/cypher/iam_can_perform_edge_writer.go), NOT from the port or family name. The template is `MATCH (p:CloudResource {uid: row.principal_uid}) MATCH (r:CloudResource {uid: row.resource_uid}) MERGE (p)-[rel:CAN_PERFORM]->(r)`, and CAN_PERFORM is a static token baked into the template (no %s: the granted action set lives in rel.actions, never in the relationship type). iamCanPerformEdgeLabel IS "CAN_PERFORM" (the const doubles as the relationship type and the statement-metadata tag); "IAM_CAN_PERFORM" appears nowhere in code, so the type is read off the template, never derived from the port or family name. The relationship MERGEs on its two endpoint nodes alone, so there is no identity block. evaluation_scope is SET after the MERGE as a plain string and is asserted here as a mutable property. actions and grant_sources are SET as LIST properties ("actions must be a SET list property", iam_can_perform_test.go) which the live assert-edges comparison cannot round-trip (strings-only readExpectedProperties, go/cmd/ifa/assert_edges_scan.go); they are proven offline instead, in the guard's merged-actions table check over the extractor rows plus the writer unit test pinning the SET list shape. Each endpoint is a reducer.cloudjoin.CloudResourceUID value = sha256 over account_id, region, resource_type, resource_id: account_id 123456789012 everywhere; region aws-global for the IAM principals, us-east-1 for the data-plane targets; and the (resource_type, resource_id) pairs (aws_iam_user, arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/deployer), (aws_iam_role, arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-role), (aws_s3_bucket, arn:aws:s3:::eshu-fixture-reports), (aws_kms_key, arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012), (aws_dynamodb_table, arn:aws:dynamodb:us-east-1:123456789012:table/eshu-fixture-orders). The deployer user sources two edges (source uid 8327c4a5 appears twice: once to the KMS key, once to the bucket); the ci-role sources the DynamoDB edge. Exactly three edges, all identity_policy_only: the other eleven permission facts contribute nothing on purpose -- one type-mismatched s3-on-KMS pattern refused by the catalog expected-type check, one Deny arming nothing, one conditioned statement the grant cannot trust, one NotAction statement, one uncatalogued iam:passrole, one absorbed s3 wildcard, one standalone lambda wildcard resolving ambiguous, one unscanned ghost-bucket ARN, one trust-sourced statement outside the identity fold, one ghost principal that was never scanned, and one catalogued ec2 action on the wrong target type. The unattached-observer role scans as a node but carries no statement.
